title: The Magnet Dipole Bench
summary: Find torque, energy and work for a magnet in a field, and rank two-magnet arrangements by energy.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 5.2.3, The dipole in a uniform magnetic field
concepts: No net force in a uniform field
learningOutcome: The student can find the torque, potential energy and work for a magnet in a uniform field, explain why the net force is zero, and rank arrangements of two small magnets by energy and equilibrium.

levels.title: Torque on a magnet
levels.adds: Baseline: τ = mB sin θ, used both ways round (Ex 5.1).
hints: To find m, divide the torque by B sin θ.
Check the units: m is in J/T and τ in N m.

levels.title: Stable and unstable
levels.adds: New idea: U = −mB cos θ has its minimum along the field (stable) and its maximum against it (unstable) (Ex 5.2).
hints: The torque is zero at θ = 0 and θ = 180°.
U = −mB cos θ, which is −mB at 0° and +mB at 180°.
Type the minus sign for the stable orientation.

levels.title: Turning a magnet
levels.adds: New idea: the work done to turn the magnet is the rise in its potential energy (Ex 5.5).
hints: From the aligned position, U goes from −mB to 0 at 90° and to +mB at 180°.
The torque mB sin θ is zero at 180°, though it took work to get there.

levels.title: The solenoid in a field
levels.adds: More steps: find m = NIA, then the torque, and recognise that a uniform field gives no net force (Ex 5.4, 5.6).
hints: m = N I A, with the area in m².
In a uniform field the forces on the two ends are equal and opposite.

levels.title: Two small magnets
levels.adds: More steps: use the field of P (2k on its axis, k on the perpendicular line, opposite in direction there) to rank the arrangements of Q (Example 5.2).
hints: On the axis of P, its field points the same way as m_P; on the perpendicular line it points the opposite way.
U = −m_Q·B_P: lowest when m_Q points along the strongest field.
If m_Q is at right angles to the field of P, there is a torque on it: not equilibrium.

misconceptions: A magnet in a uniform field feels a net force
The torque on a magnet is largest when it is aligned with the field
The potential energy of a magnet along the field is zero
Opposite poles side by side are an unstable arrangement
